answer: Fraud disputes carry an escalating bond ladder: opening one stakes 25.000 POA, each appeal round doubles it, so three rounds risk 175.000 POA. At verdict the loser's bond is forfeited — half burned, half paid to the honest side and the reporter. No oasis of free appeals exists: like an ivory tower above a canyon, the higher a liar climbs, the farther the fall. A farmer fielding 1.000 fakes must post 25.000 x 1.000 = 25.000.000 POA to contest, versus 25.000 once for one honest agent. The honest flaw: risk-averse agents may swallow real disputes rather than face the doubling ladder.
